helper-site-details: Enter the site’s postcode and address to accurately locate the project. Include the regular opening hours and note any site constraints such as access restrictions, parking, or safety considerations. These details will automatically appear in future tender and contract documents.
helper-client-info: Provide the client or employer’s official company details, including registration number, address, and primary contact for notices. This ensures all correspondence and contracts are correctly addressed and legally valid.
helper-main-contract: Enter the key details of the main contract, such as the Principal Contractor, Contract Dates, Retention terms, and applicable periods. These fields define the commercial structure for your subcontract agreements and can be updated later if required.
helper-insurance-req: Select the relevant insurance types and specify who is responsible—Contractor or Employer—for each. If certain packages have unique insurance arrangements, you can adjust these later at the subcontract level.
helper-addresses-notices: Add the postal and email addresses to be used for serving formal notices to both the Main Contractor and Subcontractor. These details ensure all legal and contractual communications are properly directed.
helper-key-dates: Record the key project milestones, including possession, review, and notice periods. These dates help define contractual responsibilities and will populate automatically into project and tender documentation.
helper-payment-terms: Define how and when payments will be made, including valuation frequency, payment due dates, and notice deadlines. This information supports accurate payment schedules and helps avoid disputes later in the process.
helper-legal-dispute: Specify whether liquidated damages or amendments to relevant events apply, and confirm the governing law for the contract. These inputs determine the legal framework and financial terms governing the subcontract.
helper-design-warranties: Indicate whether the subcontractor has design responsibility and whether collateral warranties are required. If applicable, include the design period and who the warranties should be issued to.
helper-commercial-terms: Confirm whether a Performance Bond or Parent Company Guarantee is required. These assurances provide additional financial security for the Main Contractor and should align with your project’s risk requirements.
helper-others: Enter the Gross Internal Area (GIA) for the project. This metric is used for reference in cost analysis and may appear in certain tender or contractual reports.
helper-your-project-team-details: Add your internal project team members and their contact details. You can either enter them manually or select from your existing C-Link team. These team details will appear on related project documentation when tenders are issued.

asite-guide-title: Select which situation applies to you:
asite-guide-projects-showing: Some projects are showing, but mine is missing
asite-guide-projects-desc: If other Asite projects are available in the dropdown, C-Link is likely connected to Asite. The missing project may not have been created in Asite yet, or C-Link may not have been given permission to view it.
asite-guide-projects-next-step: Please contact your McLaren Asite representative and ask them to confirm the project exists and that the C-Link Asite account has access.
asite-guide-projects-note: For the McLaren regional rollout, this is usually Daniel Pearce.
asite-guide-projects-preview: Hi {Mclaren Asite Representative}, I'm trying to connect a project in C-Link, but I can't see the corresponding Asite project in the dropdown. Other Asite projects are showing, so please can you confirm that this project exists in Asite and that the C-Link Asite account has permission to view it?
asite-guide-no-projects-desc: If no Asite projects appear in the dropdown, C-Link may not be able to retrieve projects from Asite. This could be a temporary Asite issue or a connection issue between C-Link and Asite.
asite-guide-no-projects-next-step: Please contact C-Link Support and include the project you were trying to create, the time the issue occurred, and a screenshot of this page.
asite-guide-no-projects-preview: Hi C-Link Support, I'm trying to create a project in C-Link, but no Asite projects are appearing in the Asite Project dropdown. Please can you check whether C-Link is currently able to connect to Asite and retrieve project data?
asite-folder-missing-help-title: Why can't I see my folder?
asite-folder-missing-help-common-reasons: Common reasons folders may not appear
asite-folder-missing-help-reason-1: The trade package folder has not been created in Asite yet.
asite-folder-missing-help-reason-2: C-Link does not have permission to view the folder.
asite-folder-missing-help-reason-3: Folder permissions have not inherited correctly.
asite-folder-missing-help-reason-4: The expected folder structure is missing or set up differently.
asite-folder-missing-help-next-step-body: Contact your McLaren Asite representative and ask them to confirm that the folder exists and that the C-Link Asite account has permission to view it.
asite-folder-missing-help-copy-intro: Copy this message to send to your Asite representative:
asite-folder-missing-help-copy-message: Hi {McLaren Asite representative name}, I'm trying to connect a trade package folder in C-Link, but the expected Asite folder is not visible. Please can you confirm that the folder exists in Asite and that the C-Link Asite account has permission to view it? The expected folder path is: 03 Commercial > Trade Packages
